headline: Medium risk: Pipecat’s shared-bus, multi-API defaults can amplify prompt, data, and workflow errors when paired with a prompt-listing agent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is a prompt/content-writing repository with no isolation or runtime guardrails shown, while agent B uses a shared bus and parses text/audio/video through many services. If A’s content is fed into B as instructions, B can be steered via shared-state channels. The interaction is inferred from docs-only evidence, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs are copied into agent_b prompts or shared bus messages, injection is plausible.
IF agent_b treats inbound text as instructions rather than data, prompt hijacking risk increases.
mitigations: Add a fixed system prompt separator before any agent_a content.
Disable shared-bus ingestion for untrusted text channels.
Require provenance tags on all agent_a-derived inputs.
Review one representative A→B message path for instruction/data separation.
requires-engineering: add content sanitization and schema validation at the bus boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A shows no network egress and no touched data classes, but agent B explicitly handles text, conversation state, analytics, and can call many third-party APIs with allowlisted egress. If A’s prompts or artifacts are routed into B, B may transmit them off-box. The shared workspace is not documented, so this is inferred and kept at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF agent_a artifacts are passed into agent_b sessions, those contents can reach external APIs.
IF agent_b is configured with any third-party STT/LLM/TTS provider, context may leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Route only redacted summaries from A to B.
Disable third-party providers in B for sensitive runs.
Confirm allowlist entries before starting a session.
Separate A and B into different workspaces.
requires-engineering: enforce per-field data-loss-prevention at B’s API adapters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent B supports multiple instances on a shared bus, while agent A has no concurrency model or write protections documented. If both are placed over the same mutable bus or workspace, conflicting writes or state overwrites are plausible. Because A’s write surface is not documented, uncertainty escalates to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same shared bus or workspace, state collisions can occur.
IF agent_a is wrapped with any write-capable adapter, conflicts become more likely.
mitigations: Assign separate bus topics or namespaces.
Run only one writer at a time during testing.
Snapshot shared state before each run.
Document ownership of each mutable resource.
requires-engineering: add locking or optimistic concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A is a content-writing/prompt source, and agent B is a real-time voice/chat framework that can consume text and drive downstream services. If B treats A’s output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations from A can cascade into spoken or API-backed actions. The pairwise pathway is plausible but not directly evidenced, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF agent_b forwards agent_a output into downstream tools without verification, errors propagate.
IF agent_a produces unverified facts or prompts, B may operationalize them.
mitigations: Insert a verification step before B acts on A output.
Require citations for factual claims from A.
Limit B to read-only rendering in pilot runs.
Log A→B transformations for review.
requires-engineering: add confidence gating before any action-taking tool call.

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or retention obligations are documented for agent A, and agent B’s docs show broad third-party API integrations plus analytics. The only concrete compliance concern is a potential policy mismatch if sensitive data is routed through B, but the profiles do not prove a regulated data class. One-agent citations are sufficient here because the risk is B-side handling, not a documented bilateral residency conflict.
conditions: IF regulated data is sent through agent_b providers, external processing obligations apply.
IF retention or logging settings differ across B integrations, policy mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to B.
Check provider retention settings before use.
Disable analytics for sensitive sessions.
Keep a short written data-handling note for the run.
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention policy enforcement per provider.
